entry.title: Change these iOS privacy settings to lock your iPhone from prying eyes
entry.content:
Macworld

iPhones are equipped with some of the best privacy protections in the industry, and unlike many rivals, Apple doesn’t make its money from selling your personal data. When you buy an iPhone or a Mac, you know your most sensitive data is safely locked away from prying eyes, even Apple’s.

But despite that, there are ways you can enhance your privacy even further by tweaking a few settings and features. Here, we’ll look at the things you can do to bolster your privacy and security on iOS, but many of these same principles apply to Apple’s other platforms. Make these changes and enable these features, and you’ll be taking some serious steps towards keeping your private info safe and secure.

Stop apps in their tracks

Foundry

Great privacy starts with ensuring the apps you use on your iPhone are behaving themselves. Before you download an app, you can check the App Store’s “nutrition labels” to learn what private information each app collects about you. Just go to the App Store page for the app in question and scroll down to the App Privacy section.

Another way you can keep apps in line is by using App Tracking Transparency. When you first open a freshly downloaded app, you’ll often be greeted with a pop-up window explaining that the app wants to “track your activity across other companies’ apps and websites.” Select the Ask App Not to Track option, and you’ll ensure it can’t follow you once you leave the app.

Finally, you can catch up on all the ways your data has been shared with apps on your iPhone by opening the Settings app and heading to Privacy & Security > App Privacy Report. This breaks down the requests made for your info–data and sensor access, network activity, and more–by various apps. You can disable or re-enable this report at the bottom of the page.

Close the windows into email and the web

Two activities tend to occupy most of the time spent on our iPhones: the web and email. They’re also two ways we can have our privacy violated. Thankfully, Apple has put measures in place to help combat that.

We’ll start with web browsing. If you use Safari, it comes with a feature called Intelligent Tracking Prevention. This blocks cross-site tracking, which is a technique used by websites and data brokers to follow you around the web in order to learn as much about you as possible. The end goal is to sell you products and personalized advertising.

Intelligent Tracking Prevention puts a stop to this by hiding your IP address, preventing these sites from building a profile of you. It’s on by default, but if you want to check, go to Settings > Apps > Safari and enable the toggle next to Prevent Cross-Site Tracking. Underneath this toggle is Hide IP Address; tap this and ensure the setting reads Trackers and Websites.

Foundry

Apple has a few other ways to protect yourself online. When you need to create an online account, you can use the Sign in with Apple option whenever it’s available. This gives you a random email address and redirects messages to your inbox, preventing your actual email address from being signed up to newsletters and spam mail without your permission. You can see which sites and apps you’ve used Sign in with Apple on by going to Settings > [Your Name] > Sign in with Apple.

If you pay for an iCloud+ subscription, you get access to a few other privacy-protecting features. That includes iCloud Private Relay, which ensures that no one (not even Apple) can see both your IP address and the sites you’re visiting at the same time. To enable it, go to Settings > [Your Name] > iCloud > Private Relay, then flip the Private Relay toggle on.

Another iCloud+ feature is Hide My Email. Like Sign in with Apple, this generates a random email address to use when signing up for a website account. The difference is that Hide My Email is offered even if a website doesn’t use Sign in with Apple, ensuring you’re never left without protection. To use it, select the Hide My Email option whenever you type in an email field. You can also use it in the Mail app by tapping the From field. To see where you’ve used it or to create a new email address, open the Settings app and head to [Your Name] > iCloud > Hide My Email.

You can keep your data under lock and key in the Mail app by using Mail Privacy Protection. According to Apple, this “Hides your IP address so senders can’t link it to your other online activity or determine your exact location. It also prevents senders from seeing if you’ve opened the email message they sent you.” You can enable it in Settings > Apps > Mail > Privacy Protection > Protect Mail Activity.

Lock it all down

What about the possibility of someone stealing your phone or one of your login credentials? For that, you need to make sure your phone and accounts are fully locked down. One of the most straightforward options is to enable Face ID, which can be done in Settings > Face ID & Passcode. This is one of the most secure ways to keep your private docs safely protected behind biometric verification.

Also, you can require two-factor authentication for your Apple Account in Settings > [Your Name] > Sign-In & Security > Two-Factor Authentication. Modern iPhones require a six-digit passcode, but you can increase this and optionally mix in alphanumeric characters in Face ID & Passcode settings by selecting “Change Passcode,” entering your PIN, then choosing Passcode Options.

Foundry

Despite requiring a passcode, your Lock Screen can still give would-be thieves and malcontents a lot of information. For example, the Control Center is accessible without entering a passcode, so someone could disable Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and cellular data, which in turn would prevent Find My from working, effectively disabling your device tracking. To prevent that, go to Settings > Face ID & Passcode, then scroll down to the Allow Access When Locked section and disable the toggle next to Control Center. While there, you might want to also disable access to Workout Health Data to keep this section of your personal info under wraps.

Speaking of thieves, new iPhones come with Stolen Device Protection by default, which requires a user to pass a biometric test (such as Face ID or Touch ID authentication) to perform certain tasks when your iPhone is in an unfamiliar location. To ensure it’s enabled, go to Settings > Face ID & Passcode > Stolen Device Protection, then make sure the toggle is on next to Stolen Device Protection.

Apple added a Lockdown Mode to iOS recently. This is for the most serious cases of compromised data, where a user suspects they are being targeted by a nation-state or other powerful actor. Hopefully you won’t need it, but if you do, you can enable it in Settings > Privacy & Security > Lockdown Mode. Note that this limits functionality for some apps and features.

Hide your location

Foundry

Your location can give away an awful lot about you, and that can often be used for nefarious purposes. That’s why you shouldn’t just hand out a blanket pass to any apps that demand to know your precise location. When an app asks for this data, think about whether it actually needs it, and only permit it if you feel it’s necessary for the app’s operation.

To see which apps have access to your location, open the Settings app and navigate to Privacy & Security > Location Services. Tap an app to see what permissions it has; you can choose between Never; Ask Next Time or When I Share; While Using the App; and Always (not every app has all of these options, but you’ll see at least a couple). You can also choose to share your precise whereabouts, or a more privacy-friendly vague location instead.

Similarly, you can see which apps have requested access to your iPhone’s camera and microphones by going to Settings > Privacy & Security, then choosing either Camera or Microphone. As with your location data, access to these sensors should be granted judiciously and only when necessary. Disable it for any apps that you don’t feel comfortable giving access to.

Stop unwanted trackers

Apple

This section is not related to you giving permission to something. Quite the opposite, in fact. We’ve seen in the press numerous instances of people using an AirTag to track (and stalk) an unwitting victim, which has obvious risks to privacy and safety. Thankfully, Apple has implemented a system that can alert you to an AirTag or other tracker that is logging your location when it shouldn’t be.

Note that this works with any AirTag, set of AirPods, Find My network accessory, or compatible Bluetooth tracker, so you should be alerted no matter what’s being used, as long as it can be used with an iPhone.

First, you need to have location services turned on in Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services. From here, tap System Services and enable both Find My iPhone and Significant Locations & Routes. Apple also says that both Bluetooth and notifications need to be switched on, and you can’t be using airplane mode. If all that’s in place, you’ll get a notification whenever your iPhone notices that an unknown AirTag or other tracker is traveling with you.

If that happens, the Find My app will show you where the tracker has been detected and the route it has taken with you. To find it, tap the alert, then select Continue > Play Sound to have the tracker buzz, if possible–follow the sound to find it. You might also see a Find Nearby option, which can also guide you to the tracker.

If the tracker you discover turns out to be an AirTag, you can hold your iPhone to the AirTag’s white side until a notification appears. Tap it to see info on the AirTag’s owner, including the last four digits of their phone number. To disable the tracker (regardless of its type) and prevent it from trailing you any further, open the Find My app and go to Items > Items Detected With You. Tap the unknown tracker, pick Instructions to Disable, then follow the on-screen instructions.

Make your iPhone a one-way street

Many apps (and Apple) collect analytics data to help improve their products. Sometimes, though, this information is also used to build a profile of you and serve you personalized ads. Whatever the case, you might want to disable that data collection to keep your privacy protected.

Foundry

To do so, go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements, then disable the toggles for any information you don’t feel comfortable sharing. Next, go back to Privacy & Security, then choose Apple Advertising and disable the toggle next to Personalized Ads. While this won’t cut down the number of ads you’ll see, it should stop Apple from gathering info on you and using it to build a profile.

entry.title: iOS 27: What’s new, what’s in the latest beta and what’s coming next
entry.content:
Macworld

Apple unveiled iOS 27 at WWDC on June 8, 2026, with the public release following on September 14. The latest update, iOS 27.2.1 arrived on November 9, with security fixes. It follows the October 26 release of iOS 27.2, which introduced further Siri AI improvements and new app features.

iOS 27 mainly focuses on three key areas: Siri AI, a rebuilt assistant with its own dedicated app; new child safety and parental controls; and system improvements designed to make everyday tasks faster and easier.

iOS 27 supports the iPhone 11 and later, plus the iPhone SE (2nd generation) and later, although some Apple Intelligence and Siri features require newer hardware.

This guide covers iOS 27’s biggest features, compatible iPhones and what’s coming in future updates. We regularly update it with the latest public release and beta developments, newly discovered features and reported problems.

What’s New in iOS 27 at a Glance

  • Siri AI: Apple’s new Siri AI combines personal context, onscreen awareness and web knowledge to deliver more natural conversations, richer answers, app actions and cross-device chat history.
  • Apple Intelligence across apps: Apple Intelligence expands across Safari, Photos, Messages, Mail, Calendar, Home and Shortcuts, adding smarter suggestions, automation, image generation and context-aware assistance.
  • Smarter Photos editing: Photos gains Spatial Reframing, Extend and an upgraded Clean Up tool, allowing users to improve composition, expand images and remove distractions more naturally.
  • Child safety and parental controls: New parental controls include Ask to Browse, Time Allowances, app schedules and enhanced Communication Safety tools. Activating the redesigned experience through Family Sharing requires every eligible family device to be running version 27 or later.
  • System Improvements: Apple has made many system operations faster and more efficient, which will be especially noticeable on older phones. Battery life may be longer, and there are dozens of small quality-of-life improvements throughout the system and its apps.
  • iPhone Handoff: iPhone Handoff in iOS 27 lets two eSIM-equipped iPhones share one number, switching calls, messages and Find My location when unlocked. It requires matching Apple Accounts and carrier support. T-Mobile offers it; Verizon and EE plan support. Fees may apply. More information below.

What’s coming in the next iOS 27 update?

Apple is testing iOS 27.3. Here are the latest beta versions and the features discovered so far.

Latest iOS 27 beta version

  • Latest developer beta: iOS 27.3 beta 2, released November 16, 2026. Revised developer beta 2 build, 24C5049f, released November 19
  • Latest public beta: iOS 27.3 public beta 2, released November 19, 2026.

Apple has begun testing iOS 27.3. Changes available for testing so far include:

  • Expanded Siri actions: Siri gains more capabilities within Apple’s apps, while developers can begin testing new integrations for third-party apps.
  • More Siri AI languages: Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish and Vietnamese are being tested.
  • Apple Intelligence in China: Initial features include Writing Tools, Visual Intelligence, Clean Up and Genmoji. Siri AI remains unavailable.
  • Redesigned Health app: The new design returns after appearing briefly during iOS 27.2 testing.
  • Siri access to Health data: Reports indicate that Siri AI can answer questions about information stored in the Health app in the iOS 27.3 beta. Privacy details still need confirmation, as Apple’s current support documentation says Health data cannot be read by Siri AI.
  • Safari’s Ask about Page: On supported devices, Siri can answer questions using an entire webpage, including content outside the visible screen, and use the results in follow-up tasks.
  • Safari Adaptive Dark Mode: An optional setting adapts bright webpages for dark mode. Users can exclude individual websites.
  • Safari vertical tabs: The beta adds a vertical tab layout on iPhone Duo, displaying tabs down the side of the screen.
  • iPhone Duo front-camera unlocking: An optional setting lets users unlock the closed phone with its front camera after recent Touch ID or passcode authentication. Touch ID is still required for Apple Pay and passwords, and after approximately 45 minutes of inactivity.
  • iPhone Duo Close to Lock: A new option under Settings > Display & Brightness lets users lock the phone by closing it.
  • iPhone Duo Reachability: Content can shift sideways to make the wider display easier to reach.
  • StandBy customization: The beta brings more color and layout options to StandBy on regular iPhones. StandBy still requires the phone to be charging. Users can touch and hold the StandBy screen to add, edit or delete a custom layout.
  • Apple Watch Audio Intelligence: Live Rewind and Siri Recap are available for testing with an Apple Watch Series 12 or Ultra 4.
  • Fitness+ Gym Strength: In the 27.3 betas, Fitness+ can build strength-training plans around your equipment, schedule and readiness, with adjustable weights and repetitions. It requires a Fitness+ subscription, watchOS 27.3 beta and an iPhone or iPad running the corresponding 27.3 beta.
  • Apple Music Selfie Sing: The beta lets Apple Music subscribers record short selfie videos with song details and synchronized lyrics. The Selfie Sing button appears in the lyrics view for compatible songs, although the supported selection is currently limited.
  • Video podcasts in Apple TV: Video episodes from Apple Podcasts are being added to the Apple TV app, with playback progress synced between the two apps.
  • More News+ puzzles: New puzzles are available for subscribers in the U.K., Australia and French Canada, with availability varying by region.
  • iCloud public-link checks: Apple says that starting with iOS 27.3, it will check photos, files and other iCloud content shared using “Anyone with the link” for harmful content. These items are accessible to Apple and aren’t end-to-end encrypted, even if Advanced Data Protection is enabled. The checks apply to items shared through this public-link option, rather than everything stored in iCloud. To restrict access to invited recipients, choose “People you choose” when sharing.

iOS 27 latest version: What’s in iOS 27.2.1

Apple released iOS 27.2.1 on November 9, 2026, addressing several security vulnerabilities affecting Messages, Bluetooth, AirPlay and other system components.

Two particularly concerning flaws in Messages could allow a remote attacker to join an iMessage group conversation and receive its messages, or enable someone added to a group to access messages sent before they joined. Apple has fixed both issues.

The update also addresses Bluetooth vulnerabilities that could allow a malicious nearby device to pair without user interaction, as well as weaknesses that could allow attackers to bypass limits on AirPlay pairing-code attempts. Another fix prevents apps from potentially accessing sensitive user information without proper authorization.

While Apple has not confirmed that these vulnerabilities have been actively exploited, users should install the update to protect their devices. To update an iPhone, go to Settings > General > Software Update.

iOS 27 version history: Every update and release date

What did iOS 27.0.1 add? The first update was iOS 27.0.1, released on September 28. It fixed unexpected restarts following failed Face ID authentication, a 2x-camera color artifact affecting iPhone 18 Pro models, and an iOS 27 touchscreen freeze triggered by opening Notification Center and Control Center simultaneously. iOS 27.0.1 also has a preventive role in a cellular problem that Apple did not mention in its published release notes. Apple confirmed that a small number of iPhone 18 Pro Max models on AT&T can lose cellular service, preventing calls, texts and data access and potentially affecting 911 calls. Some owners reported their phones dropping into SOS mode despite previously showing a strong 5G signal.

What did iOS 27.1 add? Apple released iOS 27.1 on October 23, 2026, exclusively for the iPhone Duo; other iPhone models moved directly from iOS 27.0.1 to iOS 27.2.

What did iOS 27.2 add? Apple released iOS 27.2 on October 26, 2026. It improves Siri AI’s memory and personal context, expands language support, and adds Suggestions in Messages alongside other app improvements, bug fixes and security updates. Dual Capture arrives for Group FaceTime calls, while iPhone Duo gains Apple Pencil (USB-C) support and Edge Light to illuminate your face during video calls. Shared Albums in Photos gains editable captions and comments, helps avoid duplicate photos, and provides reminders to save photos and videos before temporary albums expire. Read our iOS 27.2 guide for more details.

What features are still to come in iOS 27

At the time of the launch of iOS 27 not all of Apple’s promised features were available. Several were added in iOS 27.2, but there are still a couple that we’re waiting on.

  • Redesigned Health app: Having been removed in earlier beta testing, the new Health app design has returned in the iOS 27.3 beta.
  • Automatic password changes: The ability for the Passwords app to visit supported websites and automatically replace compromised passwords was removed shortly before release. 

What does Siri AI do in iOS 27

Apple

By far the biggest upgrade in iOS 27 is Siri AI – an entirely new architecture for Siri. Apple says it is more personal, conversational, and capable than the current assistant, with support for natural follow-up questions, personal context, onscreen awareness and up-to-date information from the web.

Siri AI features

  • More natural conversations: Siri AI can understand open-ended questions, follow-up requests and more complex natural language, making interactions feel less like issuing simple voice commands.
  • Personal context: Siri can draw on information stored in Messages, Mail, Photos and Notes to find details and answer questions. For example, you could ask it to find information buried in an old email or message.
  • Onscreen awareness: Siri can understand what you’re viewing and act on it, such as saving an address from a message, adding an event to Calendar or answering questions about an article.
  • Camera intelligence: A new Siri Camera mode lets you show Siri something through the iPhone’s camera, then ask questions or perform actions based on what it sees.
  • More capable app actions: Siri can perform tasks within apps such as Messages, Music and Reminders. It can, for example, edit a recently sent message, add a song to a playlist or handle more complex Apple Music requests.
  • Better general knowledge and web answers: Siri can use information from the web to answer questions about recent events and tackle more specific or complicated queries than before.
  • Conversation history across devices: A dedicated Siri app lets users revisit previous conversations, pin important chats and continue conversations across Apple devices using iCloud syncing.
  • More natural Siri voices: Siri gains more expressive voices, with controls on compatible devices for adjusting speaking pace and expressiveness. Voice customization requires an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air or newer.
  • Improved dictation: Better speech recognition, automatic punctuation, capitalization and formatting allow users to dictate more naturally when converting speech into text.
  • AI-assisted message replies: Siri can compose contextual replies in Messages using the conversation, personal information and web searches. Shortcuts can also automate replies to selected contacts, although manual Siri-assisted replies allow users to check and edit the response before it is sent.

iOS 27.2 added several further Siri AI improvements:

  • Recall information from previous conversations.
  • Use Messages photo attachments, Calendar attendees and voicemails, with better results from Safari history and Reading List.
  • Control app access for Siri, Search and suggestions through Excluded Apps.
  • Select and copy individual portions of Siri’s responses.

iOS 27.3 expands Siri’s actions across Apple apps, including Calendar, Messages, Music and Reminders. You can ask Siri what it can do within an app.

Apple has also opened a developer preview that lets third-party apps connect their content and actions to Siri AI. This requires developers to build support into their apps. Apple says App Store submissions using these capabilities will open in spring, so installing iOS 27.3 alone will not enable the new integrations across existing apps.

If you haven’t got Siri AI yet find out how here: Why don’t I have Siri AI on my iPhone?

Read about what happened when we made Siri AI Answer all our Messages.

How good is Siri AI?

Siri AI represents a significant improvement over the old Siri, particularly when handling conversational questions, current information, and personal context. It also has a dedicated app where you can see and continue previous conversations, upload images or documents, and more.

Even in our early tests during the beta, Siri AI proved to be much more helpful and useful.

It’s definitely one of the biggest reasons to upgrade to iOS 27, potentially changing Siri from a basic voice-command system into a more general way of interacting with the iPhone.

Apple’s approach to AI safety also appears more restrained than some rival chatbots, with Siri designed to avoid excessive flattery, pretending to be human, or responding inappropriately to potentially harmful requests.

Siri AI remains a beta feature. iOS 27.2 added French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish alongside English. Siri AI remains unavailable on iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch in the EU and mainland China. The EU restriction does not apply to Siri AI on Mac so Siri AI can be used on the Mac in the EU.

Regional Siri AI availability

Siri AI will not initially be available on iPhone or iPad in the EU. It will also remain unavailable in China while Apple works through regulatory issues.

The first release only supported the English language, and initially had only Expressive Voices for English (UK) and English (US). Support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish arrived with iOS 27.2.

Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish and Vietnamese support is being tested in the iOS 27.3 beta. Siri AI is still not available in mainland China.

Lack of Siri language support is separate to Apple Intelligence language support.

Siri AI compatibility

Siri AI requires iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, and all iPhone 16 models and later, and the “new expressive voices” feature requires an iPhone 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max, iPhone Air, iPhone 18 Pro or 18 Pro Max and currently supports US and UK English voices.

Siri AI age restriction: Siri AI is unavailable to children under 13.

Apple Intelligence across apps

As well as Siri AI, the enhanced Apple Intelligence will power new features in Apple’s core apps throughout iOS 27. Safari can organize tabs into topics, monitor webpages for changes and even build extensions from natural-language descriptions. Photos gains a new Spatial Reframing editing tools including an upgraded Clean Up feature. Messages, Mail, and Calendar can now understand context, suggest actions and create events from simple descriptions.

Usage limits: Some cloud-based Apple Intelligence features have daily allowances, including advanced Siri AI requests, intelligent photo editing, Image Playground and cloud models in Shortcuts. Within the iOS 27.3 beta, Apple has detailed higher allowances through eligible iCloud+ plans:

50GB: Standard device limit
200GB: Up to 2× the standard device limit
2TB: Up to 5× the standard device limit
6TB: Up to 10× the standard device limit
12TB: Up to 20× the standard device limit

Apple has not disclosed the number of requests included in the standard allowance. Each device has its own standard limits; additional iCloud+ capacity is shared across devices and participating family members. Basic Siri requests remain available after the advanced-request allowance is exhausted.

Regional restrictions apply: Apple says increased access through iCloud+ is unavailable in the U.K., EU, Brazil and South Korea, with increased Apple Intelligence access also unavailable in China.

In testing the 27.3 beta software, Macworld’s Mahmoud Itani encountered Siri AI’s daily usage limit after roughly 20 minutes of making requests on Apple TV, despite having a 2TB iCloud+ subscription. His iPad and Mac subsequently displayed warnings that they were approaching their limits.

New features coming to apps in iOS 27

iOS 27 brings a mix of major Apple Intelligence upgrades and smaller quality-of-life improvements across Safari, Photos, Messages, AirPods, Passwords, Wallet, and other core iPhone apps. Apple is also making iOS more adaptable to different screen sizes and orientations, which are changes necessary for the iPhone Duo.

Safari

Safari can automatically group open tabs into topics, making related pages easier to find. A new Notify Me feature will monitor webpages and alert you to changes such as price drops or products coming back into stock.

There’s also a new Describe an Extension feature which lets users create custom Safari extensions simply by explaining what they want the extension to do.

In the iOS 27.3 beta, Safari gains Ask about Page on supported devices. This lets Siri draw on the entire webpage, including sections you haven’t scrolled to. For example, you can ask Siri to extract a packing list from a travel guide, then save it in Notes.

Apple

Photos

Photos gains significantly more powerful AI editing tools.

Reframe can alter the composition and perspective of an existing photo, while Extend generates new image content beyond the original frame when straightening a horizon or changing the aspect ratio.

Apple

Clean Up has also been improved, with Fast and High Quality modes for removing unwanted objects or details. High Quality mode can produce considerably more natural results, although more ambitious edits can still introduce distortions or invented details.

Photos also adds new categories and the ability to save a frame from a video as a full-resolution photo. The resulting HEIF or JPG retains the video’s original resolution, date, and location metadata rather than simply creating a screenshot.

Camera

iOS 27 features a new more customizable camera interface that lets you pin the controls you use most often. For the iPhone 18 Pro, there are also “pro controls” like white balance, shutter speed, and manual focus along with Apple Reference Image, an authentication system designed to prove that a photo or video was genuinely captured on an iPhone and has not subsequently been manipulated.

The new Siri mode in the Camera app is a more convenient and logical way to access the Visual Intelligence features that used to require either a long-press of the camera button or a Control Center button.

Messages

Foundry

Messages gets several useful improvements.

You can decide what the microphone button beside the text field does. Under Settings > Apps > Messages > Show in Text Field, it can be set to Record Audio, Start Dictation, or None. Disabling it does not remove either feature: dictation remains available from the keyboard and audio messages remain in the + menu.

Voice-message playback controls are easier to access.

iOS 27.2 adds Suggestions in Messages, which uses the context of your conversations to suggest actions in apps such as Calendar and Reminders. For example, when you discuss dinner plans, Messages can suggest creating a Calendar invitation.

Messages in iOS 27 will gain smarter suggested replies that can better reflect the user’s writing style. (This was removed from the iOS 27 beta and wasn’t available at the launch of iOS 27).

Drawing

Foundry

A new dedicated Drawing app replaces the old hidden handwriting interface. Accessible from the + menu, it uses the familiar pens, colours and drawing controls found in Notes and Markup, with finished drawings sent as images.

Mail

Mail gains more context-aware smart replies, including responses that can better match the user’s usual writing style.

Apple Intelligence can also surface information from Mail elsewhere in iOS. For example, the Phone app could retrieve a flight confirmation number from an email when you call an airline.

Phone

A new Call Context feature can surface information that may be useful when on a call. Apple says the information is selected according to who you are calling rather than by listening to the conversation. For example, calling an airline could cause iOS to surface the relevant flight confirmation from Mail.

Birthday reminders can also appear when calling contacts whose birthdays are stored on the iPhone.

iPhone Handoff

iPhone Handoff in iOS 27 lets you switch between two iPhones while keeping the same phone number. The number is active on only one iPhone at a time. When you unlock one of the two iPhones, your calls, voicemail, messages—including SMS and RCS—and your Find My location will be linked to that iPhone.

The feature will work on any iPhone running iOS 27, as long as it has an eSIM. Both phones must use the same Apple Account, with Messages in iCloud enabled and matching FaceTime/iMessage sign-ins.

You will need a carrier and eligible plan that specifically support iPhone Handoff – an ordinary eSIM plan alone isn’t enough. In the U.S. T-Mobile offers iPhone Handoff for $5 a month and Verizon has announced support for later in 2026. In the U.K. EE has announced that support for iPhone Handoff is coming soon for £5 a month.

FaceTime

Dual Capture arrived in iOS 27.2, allowing Group FaceTime participants to share front- and rear-camera views simultaneously.

iOS 27.2 also adds support for bringing a third-party sign language interpreter or live captioner into a FaceTime call, providing additional communication support for participants.

Passwords

Apple

The Passwords app continues to warn about weak, reused and compromised credentials, but iOS 27 will go a step further – eventually. Automatic password changes are coming to the Passwords app in a future software update. Apple has not confirmed a release date.

The forthcoming feature will, with your permission, visit supported websites, change vulnerable passwords and save the replacement credentials automatically. See: Apple got rid of my biggest password headache.

The usefulness of the feature will depend on how widely websites are supported and how well it handles obstacles such as two-factor authentication and unusual account-management interfaces.

Apple removed this ability to detect compromised passwords and replace them from the beta shortly before the release of iOS 27. It’s expected to arrive with a later update.

Shortcuts

Shortcuts gains Describe a Shortcut, allowing users to create automations simply by explaining what they want to happen.

Apple Intelligence interprets the request and assembles the appropriate actions across supported apps, potentially making Shortcuts significantly easier to use for people unfamiliar with building automations manually.

Calendar

Calendar can create or modify events from natural-language instructions.

Apple says the app can recognize contacts, locations, dates and other event details as users type, reducing the amount of information that needs to be entered manually.

Siri can also create complete Calendar entries for information that is on your screen in that moment, or by taking a picture with the Siri mode in the Camera app.

Image Playground

Image Playground is considerably more powerful and realistic.

Apple says it can create photorealistic images and lets users modify generated pictures simply by describing the changes they want. Individual objects can also be selected, resized, or repositioned.

iOS 27.2 adds SynthID support to help identify images generated or modified using Photos and Image Playground.

Wallet

Wallet can create custom passes from QR codes.

Users can add their own fields and information to the pass, and passes automatically sync to Apple Watch.

Weather

Weather gets a clearer, more detailed forecast interface, with rearranged information tiles and new 10-day views showing precipitation probability/amount and wind speed throughout each day.

Home app

Apple Intelligence comes to the Home app for compatible HomeKit Secure Video cameras. It can group related camera notifications, describe recorded video and highlight clips that appear particularly noteworthy.

Maps

Apple Maps improves Flyover using higher-quality aerial imagery and Visual Intelligence models.

Apple says this produces sharper architectural detail and more realistic rendering of elements such as individual trees.

Apple News+

In the iOS 27.3 beta, Apple News+ subscribers in the U.K. gain a daily quick crossword, crossword mini and Sudoku. Australian subscribers gain those puzzles plus Quartiles and Emoji Game, while French-Canadian subscribers gain Quartiles and Emoji Game.

Podcasts

Video podcasts become easier to use, with improved controls for switching between watching a podcast and simply listening to it.

iOS 27.2 also reorganizes the Podcasts app’s Home tab into two separate sections: New Episodes, where you can find the latest releases from shows you follow, and Continue Playing, where you can resume episodes you’ve already started. This makes it easier to distinguish new listening from unfinished episodes.

Fitness

Workout summaries have been redesigned to make them easier to share.

Users can also hide completed Fitness+ workouts.

Games

iOS 27.2 improves the Games app’s Friends tab with more information about suggested friends. Friends’ player pages also show the games they’ve played recently, making it easier to find something to play together.

Apple TV

iOS 27.2 adds Simple Profiles to the Apple TV app, allowing members of your household to have their own profiles with recommendations tailored to their viewing preferences.

The iOS 27.3 beta also adds video podcast episodes from Apple Podcasts to the Apple TV app, giving viewers another place to discover and watch them.

iOS 27 changes beyond the iPhone

CarPlay

CarPlay gains an audio scrubber, giving drivers and passengers more direct control when moving through audio tracks and other content.

AirPods

iOS 27 introduces several new AirPods features.

A new Custom EQ lets users independently adjust bass, mids and treble using a simple three-band equalizer under Settings > AirPods > Audio and Routing > Equalizer > Custom.

Compatible AirPods also gain improved Precision Finding through Find My, making individual earbuds easier to locate.

Some features require both iOS 27 and compatible AirPods firmware.

Read How to tune your AirPods with a custom EQ in iOS 27.

Other changes in iOS 27

It’s not only individual apps that are seeing changes.

Home Screen and landscape mode

Apple is making iOS significantly more flexible when dealing with different screen orientations and sizes.

More Apple apps now work properly in landscape, including Health, Home, Music, Weather, and Watch. Dynamic Island and Live Activities can also adapt to landscape orientation. The Home Screen supports extra-large widgets.

These changes could simply improve iPhone usability, but they’re also well suited to Apple’s folding iPhone Duo.

iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 has similarly become freely resizable, with Apple apps dynamically rearranging their interfaces as the window changes shape.

Liquid Glass refinements

Apple

Apple says Liquid Glass has been refined for better readability, more uniform refraction and improved contrast. A new slider lets users adjust the look from ultraclear to fully tinted, while updated icons, toolbars, sidebars and window shapes add polish.

Ringtones, alarms and alert volume

iOS 27 finally separates several sound-volume controls.

Instead of one combined Ringtone and Alerts slider, users can independently adjust:

  • Ringtones
  • Alarms and timers
  • Alerts and system sounds

The change is optional. Under Settings > Sounds & Haptics, turning off Match Ringtone Volume reveals separate controls.

Media and call volume continue to work independently as before.

Keyboard

iOS 27 introduces a new quick-paste control above the keyboard.

It lets you paste recently copied text, images or screenshots without having to long-press inside a text field, making everyday copy-and-paste considerably faster.

Apple has also made the Liquid Glass keyboard design more consistent across apps.

Privacy and Find My

iOS 27 introduces the ability to temporarily pause Find My location sharing without notifying the person with whom the location is normally shared.

Recovery and troubleshooting

Apple is also expanding the iPhone’s recovery interface, giving users more options for diagnosing problems and recovering an iPhone without immediately connecting it to another device.

System changes and how iOS 27 makes your iPhone faster

Alongside the headline AI features, Apple says iOS 27 includes a wide range of under-the-hood improvements designed to make iPhones faster, smoother and more efficient.

Apps can launch up to 30% faster, newly taken photos can appear in the Photos library up to 70% faster, and AirDrop transfers can be up to 80% quicker. External drive transfers should also improve, while updates to network performance and the system-wide search index are designed to make connectivity and finding information faster.

The company has also reworked core technologies including CPU scheduling, display performance and processing efficiency. These changes should benefit older iPhones in particular, with Apple promising smoother performance and more efficient battery use on devices as old as the iPhone 11 and second-generation iPhone SE.

Our testing of the iOS 27 beta supports those claims. On an iPhone 11 Pro Max, Camera launch time fell from 0.98 seconds in iOS 26 to 0.65 seconds in iOS 27, while Maps improved from 3.01 seconds to 1.36 seconds.

Everyday use also feels smoother, with more fluid animations, unlocking, Control Center and app transitions. The phone ran cooler during testing too, which could point to improved system efficiency and potentially better battery performance.

More broadly, iOS 27 appears focused on refinement rather than simply adding new features. Apple says it has addressed dozens of common user frustrations, while changes such as more adjustable Liquid Glass effects are intended to improve readability and general usability.

That focus should make iOS 27 particularly worthwhile for owners of older iPhones, even on models that do not support Siri AI. Those devices still gain performance improvements alongside features such as clipboard tools for the keyboard, independent alarm and timer volume controls, custom Wallet passes, Photos changes, larger widgets, and Liquid Glass refinements.

Child safety and parental controls

Apple

There are lots of improvements to parental controls, including new time allowances for entertainment, games, and social media, and new schedule tools for different times of day or days of the week.

This includes new features like an expansion of the existing “ask to buy” feature for apps to websites. Before a child can view a new website, they’ll have to ask for permission.

Ask to Browse: Will expand the current Ask to Buy feature to the web. Children will need to request permission before visiting new websites, and parents can review requests in Messages before approving.

Communication Safety: Communication Safety continues to help protect children from viewing or sharing nudity in Messages, FaceTime and other apps. Apple says it will also intervene before children see gore or violent content in shared images and videos.

Time Allowances and schedules: Parents can set Time Allowances across categories such as Entertainment, Games and Social Media. Recommendations are based on a child’s age combined with guidance from clinical and child development experts. Schedules let parents choose which apps are available at different times or on different days.

Redesigned Screen Time: Screen Time gets a redesigned interface with an at-a-glance view of average device usage and most-used apps. Apple says parents can quickly limit or extend access in the moment.

Child accounts and family safety: Apple says child accounts remain central to age-appropriate protections. Parents can manage app access, web access, communication permissions and Screen Time settings.

Problems with Parental Control setup

Updating the parent’s iPhone is not enough to activate the redesigned Screen Time experience. Apple says every eligible iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch and Vision Pro in the Family Sharing group must be running the appropriate version 27 software.

Devices that cannot run version 27 are listed as Legacy Devices and can continue using the older Screen Time and Family Sharing system. Apple says these incompatible devices should not prevent supported devices from adopting the new controls.

To find out which devices need to be updated go to Settings > Family > View Family Devices. Once eligible devices are running iOS 27, go to Settings > Family > Get Started to transfer the family’s existing parental controls or set up new ones.

Some families have encountered delays, outdated device listings and eligible hardware incorrectly appearing not to have been updated. Apple has acknowledged the rollout problems and says it is working to resolve them. If an eligible device is no longer owned or accessible, Apple recommends removing it from the Apple Account device list.

Accessibility changes in iOS 27

Accessibility features are smarter and more intuitive in iOS 27:

  • VoiceOver gives richer image descriptions and better understanding of onscreen content.
  • Live Recognition lets users press the Action button to ask questions about their surroundings and receive detailed responses.
  • Voice Control is more intuitive, allowing users to describe onscreen buttons and controls rather than remembering exact coordinate labels or numbers.
  • Accessibility Reader is able to handle more complex source material and provide summaries and translation.

iOS 27 compatibility

Roman Loyola/IDG

According to Apple, iOS 27 supports iPhones back to the iPhone 11 and second-generation iPhone SE, although some Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features require newer hardware.

Support for iOS 27 does not mean every device gets every feature. Apple Intelligence and Siri AI require an iPhone 15 Pro or iPhone 16 or later, while the most advanced on-device AI models require an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air, or iPhone 18 Pro. On iPad, Apple Intelligence requires an M1-class model or the A17 Pro iPad mini, while the newest on-device models require an M4 iPad with at least 12GB of RAM.

There had been speculation that the iPhone 11 series and iPhone SE 2 would miss out on iOS 27 after leaker Instant Digital claimed on Weibo that the 2019 iPhone 11, 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max, along with the 2020 iPhone SE 2, would no longer be supported. That prediction proved incorrect, giving those models at least one more year of software support.

However, the iPhone 11 generation is nearing the end of its support life. As we explain in our guide to how long Apple supports iPhones, the iPhone 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max have already been added to Apple’s Vintage iPhone list.

The iOS 27 compatibility list is:

  • iPhone 18 Pro
  • iPhone 18 Pro Max
  • iPhone Duo
  • iPhone 17e (launched in 2026)
  • iPhone 17, 17 Pro / 17 Pro Max (launched in 2025)
  • iPhone Air (launched in 2025)
  • iPhone 16e (launched in 2025)
  • iPhone 16 / 16 Plus and iPhone 16 Pro / 16 Pro Max (launched in 2024)
  • iPhone 15 / 15 Plus and iPhone 15 Pro / 15 Pro Max (launched in 2023)

entry.title: U.K. government ordered to reveal secret Apple backdoor demand
entry.content:
Macworld

The U.K.’s Investigatory Powers Tribunal today ruled that the British government must confirm that it demanded access to Apple customers’ data in 2025.

Early last year, the Washington Post was tipped off about the secret order, or “technical capability notice,” which ordered Apple to “create a back door allowing [U.K. authorities] to retrieve all the content any Apple user worldwide has uploaded to the cloud.” At the time, we warned that such an order would instantly compromise the security of more than two billion Apple users across the globe.

Apple resisted, choosing to remove the ADP feature from U.K. iPhones rather than comply with the order, and it was subsequently reported that British politicians had given up on the scheme. But while it was common knowledge that the attempt had been made, the Home Office refused to acknowledge this, arguing that revealing the existence of the order would damage national security and the public interest.

Apple itself was not permitted to disclose that it had received a technical capability notice. Until now the company has adhered to this even while commenting in carefully non-specific terms on the situation. At one point, for example, it stated that “we have never built a backdoor or master key to any of our products, and we never will” without actually confirming it had been ordered to do so in this case.

But now, finally, as TechCrunch reports, the national security argument has been put to rest.

Having noted that “anyone with even a passing interest in this topic already knows that the respondent has served a technical capability notice on Apple,” the three judges indicate that they “reject the respondent’s contention that it would be damaging to national security to confirm the fact that the respondent has given Apple a technical capability notice.”

It should be noted that this judgment refers to the existence of the order rather than its specific details. The judges say this is “another matter” which “is better addressed separately.” The case, in other words, is not finished yet.

entry.title: Apple is Building an AI Agent That Can Use Apps and Code
entry.content:
Apple is working on a proactive AI agent like Meta's Muse or OpenAI's Dots, according to job listings spotted by Bloomberg.


The listing describes an AI agent that can code, use apps, and browse the web.
Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does. It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step. It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple. Our team is building the foundation for that future, and we're looking for a senior engineering leader to make it real.

Apple's listing notes that safety, privacy, and security need to be "central to the design" of its agentic AI. Apple is seeking someone who can work across the Siri, UI frameworks, and Apple Foundation Models teams, joining a group already working on "general-purpose computer-use agents."
People already do their most valuable work by moving fluidly between tools: a browser, a document, a terminal, an editor, a service. We're building AI agents that can do the same. We're a team of engineers, AI applied researchers, and systems specialists working on general-purpose computer-use agents. These agents plan and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs, and they can coordinate specialized sub-agents along the way.

Bloomberg previously said Apple was aiming to make ‌Siri‌ "more like an agent" as soon as 2027. With almost every major AI company adopting proactive AI, it makes sense that Apple is rushing to create a competitive product.

Meta came out with its Muse agent in September, and the app quickly shot up the App Store charts. OpenAI followed with Dots, Anthropic launched Claude Duet, and Google turned its Gemini Spark agent into "Tasks" and added new features. All of the proactive agents offer to do tasks for users without being asked, which isn't something ‌Siri‌ AI is capable of.

New Apple CEO John Ternus has reportedly been pushing software engineering chief Craig Federighi to move faster on AI.

entry.title: I already hit Apple’s ‘generous’ daily Siri AI usage limit
entry.content:
Macworld

You’re probably vaguely familiar with AI chatbots’ usage limits or tokens, which are dictated by your plan and the type of requests you make. When you hit a limit, you typically need to wait for a few hours or days until full functionality is restored. 

In the meantime, your queries are handled by a less capable model that may not be as fast or accurate. While Siri AI on iOS 27 operates similarly, we haven’t had to deal with usage limits until iOS 27.3, when Apple rolled out daily usage limits based on iCloud storage tiers. However, unlike other services, Apple hasn’t been very clear about how tokens are tallied. So imagine my surprise when I hit one with a relatively simple workflow, despite subscribing to the 2TB iCloud+ plan, which multiplies the quota by 5X. It’s still unclear what the limits are, but they appear to be significantly more stringent than those of other platforms I’ve used.

It all started when I was working on an upcoming Macworld article revolving around Siri AI on Apple TV. Over the course of 20 minutes, I made numerous straightforward Siri requests on tvOS once every minute or so. Most of them were as simple as “send my friend a text,” while the more complex tasks included surfacing iPhone file names and reminders on the big screen and installing an app. Neither I nor the other family members on my account had generated any media in Image Playground (does anyone?), nor had we used Siri to solve any deeply analytical problems or used any third-party apps or shortcuts that rely on Apple’s AI models.

Interestingly, Apple claims that Siri AI includes a “generous daily usage limit” for all users, whether or not they subscribe to iCloud+. So one would assume that the 5x increase included with my $9.99/month 2TB iCloud+ plan would be sufficient for direct questions, basic commands, minimal proofreading, and the like. Apparently not. The Siri app now displays a “daily limit reached” banner on my iPhone, barring me from making any advanced requests until tomorrow.

For reference, advanced requests include plain multi-step queries such as “check the weather and text it to my mom.” Instead, I now have to ask about the forecast and have it send the message separately—as the downgraded Siri experience cannot handle the complexity of both at once for the rest of the day—or upgrade to the $29.99/month 6TB iCloud+ plan. 

Meanwhile, my iPad and Mac now also warn that I’m approaching their respective daily request limits, as my iPhone and Apple TV have seemingly exhausted the shared pool. That’s by far the most restrictive limit I’ve ever encountered with any other popular AI chatbot. So unless you’re spending a fortune on iCloud each month, be careful with how much you talk to Siri—it could cost you.

entry.title: iPhone Duo vs. Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8: Which is Better?
entry.content:
A couple of months before the iPhone Duo came out, Samsung launched the Galaxy Z Fold8. It's Samsung's widest and shortest foldable to date, with Samsung adopting an aspect ratio closer to the ‌iPhone Duo‌'s than its previous foldable smartphones. Since the Z Fold8 was clearly designed to compete with the ‌iPhone Duo‌, we thought we'd compare the two devices.

Subscribe to the MacRumors YouTube channel for more videos.

The Galaxy Z Fold8 and ‌iPhone Duo‌ are similar in size, but the Fold8 is noticeably lighter. It's about 50 grams lighter than the ‌iPhone Duo‌, and it makes a difference when you're holding it. It's lighter because it's thinner than the ‌iPhone Duo‌ when folded and unfolded. The Z Fold8 is 6mm taller and around 3mm narrower, though both have a 7.6-inch inner display.

The ‌iPhone Duo‌ has a heftier feel and a more premium build, plus it has rounded corners that feel nicer in the hand than the Z Fold8's sharper, rectangular corners.

Apple used a matte nano-texture display for the ‌iPhone Duo‌, and that's likely something we're going to see Android smartphone makers imitate in their future foldables. The matte display goes a long way toward minimizing the visibility of the crease. Apple also put the camera on the inner display under the screen, which is something Samsung experimented with in earlier models and then abandoned.

Under-display front cameras are generally lower resolution than standard cameras, and there have been complaints about the quality of the ‌iPhone Duo‌'s inner front camera. The Z Fold8 has a more traditional hole-punch camera that's better quality.

Both smartphones use fingerprint recognition rather than facial recognition, but Samsung has long offered a face unlock feature that uses the front-facing camera. Apple just this week adopted a similar face unlock option, and it's coming in iOS 27.3. Face unlock is less secure than the Face ID system used for Apple's other iPhones, but it is more convenient than Touch ID for some users.

Neither smartphone has a telephoto camera, so both Apple and Samsung compromised on camera quality. The ‌iPhone Duo‌ has a 48-megapixel Main camera and a 48-megapixel Ultra Wide, while the Z Fold8 has 50-megapixel wide and ultra wide cameras. The main difference in image quality is the computational processing each smartphone offers, so which one is "better" comes down to your preference for white balance, saturation, tone, and similar factors.

The Z Fold8 supports 8K video recording and reverse wireless charging for accessories, plus it has a physical SIM while the Duo only has an eSIM. Samsung's smartphone is limited to IP48 dust and water resistance, while the ‌iPhone Duo‌ has IP68. Samsung uses the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, and the ‌iPhone Duo‌ has Apple's A20 Pro chip. The other big difference is stylus support. The ‌iPhone Duo‌ works with the USB-C Apple Pencil, but the Z Fold8 doesn't work with Samsung's S Pen options.

Since Samsung has been making foldable smartphones for years, developers have had more time to update their apps for the form factor. Most Android apps already work well, while we're still waiting for many developers to update their apps for the Duo. Samsung is also ahead on multitasking, with the option to use three apps at once and support for pop-up windows and a taskbar.

Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold8 is slightly cheaper than the ‌iPhone Duo‌, with pricing starting at $1,899.99 while the Duo starts at $1,999, but deciding between them will come down to your operating system preference and device ecosystem. If you're accustomed to iOS and have an Apple Watch, Mac, and other Apple devices, there's little reason to choose a Samsung smartphone. The same goes for Samsung users who have other Galaxy devices.

Do you prefer the ‌iPhone Duo‌ or the Galaxy Z Fold8? Let us know in the comments below.

entry.title: The iMac might be stuck with an LCD forever
entry.content:
Macworld

Apple’s devices are slowly switching over to OLED displays. It started with the Apple Watch, then the iPhone X and the iPad Pro, and most recently OLED finally made it to the Mac with the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display. It’s been a long process that started with smaller devices and has gradually made its way into larger ones, but according to The Elec, it’s going to be a while before we see OLED in Apple’s biggest screens.

According to the report, Apple is considering either delaying or canceling its plans for an OLED iMac. The reason: OLED panels that meet Apple’s standards are too expensive right now. Since Apple’s all-in-one “sells in smaller volumes than smartphones or laptops,” it’s been more difficult to “maintain competitive pricing if expensive OLED panels are adopted,” according to The Elec.

Another reason that may have influenced Apple’s decision is the sales of the iPad Pro, which was upgraded in 2024 with a tandem OLED display. OLED’s higher cost cause the iPad Pro’s price to increase, which The Elec says resulted in “sales below expectations.” And more more reason for the change of plans is that Apple’s new CEO, John Ternus, is “reassessing the commercial viability” of OLED.

When Apple introduced the OLED iPad in 2024, the price increased $200. The 11-inch iPad Pro before OLED was $799, then in 2024 it increased to $999, while the 13-inch iPad Pro jumped from $1,099 to $1,299. Similarly Apple’s new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is $400 more than the MacBook Pro with a mini-LED display. Compounding things is the RAM and storage shortages, which have pushed iPad and Mac prices even higher. Apple just released the M6 iMac without increasing the price further.

iMac development hasn’t shut down completely. The Elec states that Apple has plans for a new LCD-based model based on the current display technology for “around 2029,” which would likely be an M8 chip. Perhaps by then, the cost for OLED will have come down, and Apple can revisit its iMac OLED plans for 2030, but you probably shouldn’t get your hopes up.

entry.title: Best AirPods Black Friday deals 2026: Our picks for Pro, standard AirPods and Max

PRICES CHECKED NOVEMBER 19 2026 – Deals change quickly, so we will update this page throughout November

Black Friday is a great time to buy AirPods, with retailers competing to offer discounts across Apple’s earbuds and over-ear headphones. Previous sales have brought substantial savings on established models, clearance bargains on older generations, and even discounts on newly released AirPods. But the biggest percentage saving doesn’t necessarily mean the best buy: an older pair needs to be sufficiently cheaper than its replacement to justify missing out on newer features.

Last Black Friday, standard AirPods 4 briefly dropped to $69 in the U.S., while the noise-canceling version fell to $99 – an $80 saving. Even the then-new AirPods Pro 3 received a discount of around $30, while older AirPods Pro 2 reached approximately $139 before selling out. AirPods Max were available for around $400, roughly $150 below their regular price. U.K. savings were more modest, with AirPods 4 at £99 and AirPods Pro 2 at £169, although stock frequently ran out.

This year, we’d watch AirPods Pro 3 and AirPods Max 2 for meaningful discounts, while remaining AirPods 4 and AirPods Pro 2 stock could bring some of the biggest clearance savings. The recently released AirPods 5 may see smaller reductions, making it especially important to compare their price with discounted Pro models. Below, we explain which AirPods to choose and how the offers compare with previous discounts. For savings on Macs, iPads, Apple Watch and more, see our best Apple Black Friday deals.

Apple’s owb Black Friday offer runs November 27–30, 2026. Buy eligible AirPods directly from Apple and you’ll receive a gift card to use on a future purchase. More details here: Apple Black Friday 2026: Up to $300/£240 in gift cards – full list of eligible products.

Which AirPods should you buy this Black Friday?

AirPods Pro 3 – Our best overall choice

Apple

AirPods Pro 3 are especially worth considering if you want strong noise cancellation, a secure in-ear fit, or Apple’s hearing-health features. Their foam-infused ear tips help improve the fit, while an in-ear heart-rate sensor adds another reason to choose them over standard AirPods. Battery life is rated at up to eight hours with noise cancellation enabled.

For most buyers looking for noise-isolating earbuds, these would be our first choice. Older AirPods Pro 2 are worth considering only when the clearance savings are substantial.

U.S. Black Friday price: Amazon has already slashed almost $70 off the AirPods Pro 3, but we expect the price to go lower. We hope they’ll return to their all-time low of $169 by Black Friday.

U.K. Black Friday price: Earlier in November, AirPods Pro 3 were £30 off in the U.K., before rising to £200, then dropping down to £174, only to return to £200. This is one to watch because that price is going up and down like a Swanee whistle. Apple’s £40 gift card offers better value currently.

Apple’s deal: You can get a $50/£40 gift card with your purchase.

AirPods 5 – Best for buyers who prefer earbuds without silicone tips

Apple

AirPods 5 offer a lower-cost entry point and an open-ear design for people who don’t like silicone-tipped earbuds. They include Active Noise Cancellation as standard, alongside Transparency mode and Adaptive Audio.

Check which charging case you’re buying. The Wireless Charging Case package adds wireless charging, longer battery life, a Find My speaker, and volume adjustment by swiping the stems. It’s our preferred package when the price difference is small.

U.S. Black Friday price: We’ve not seen a discount yet on the AirPods 5.

U.K. Black Friday price: You can get £20 off the AirPods 5 in the U.K. This is the same ‘saving’ as Apple’s gift card, but you get the £20 saving upfront.

Apple’s deal: Get $25/£20 gift card with the purchase of AirPods 5.

AirPods Max 2 – Best for over-ear listening

Apple

AirPods Max 2 are the option to consider if you specifically want over-ear headphones. The March 2026 update introduced Apple’s H2 chip and improved noise cancellation, while retaining the premium design and a choice of colors.

We find them difficult to recommend at full price, so the size of the discount matters. Compare any offer with previous sale prices rather than judging it solely against Apple’s asking price.

U.S. Black Friday price: Amazon has the AirPods Max 2 for $449, that’s $99 off. They could still go lower though.

U.K. Black Friday price: The AirPods Max 2 are £449 at Amazon – that’s £50 off. You can get the same deal at AO and Boots. Apple’s £60 gift card offers better value, currently.

Apple’s deal: Get $75/£60 gift card with the purchase of AirPods Max 2.

Other AirPods – Buy only at a worthwhile clearance price

Apple

AirPods 4 and AirPods Pro 2 can still be worth considering, but compare them with the discounted prices of their replacements. A large reduction from an older model’s launch price can disguise a small saving over a newer, more capable pair.

Check the exact generation, charging case, condition, and seller before buying. For more help choosing, read our AirPods buying guide.

U.S. Black Friday price: There’s $150 off the former price of the AirPods Pro 2 at Walmart, meaning you can grab a pair for just $149.

U.K. Black Friday price: You can get the AirPods 4 with ANC for £109 at John Lewis – but that’s only £10 less than AirPods 5, so we’d recommend waiting for that price to go even lower.

Other headphones – Worthy AirPods alternatives

Beats

If AirPods aren’t in your budget, Apple also sells a line of Beats headphones and earbuds that offer many of the same features for a lower price, including the popular on-ear Solo 4 and Powerbeats Pro 2. We’ll also track headphone deals in our roundup of the best earbuds for iPhone and best over-ear headphones if you’d like to see deals on other brands.

U.S. Black Friday price: There is $100 off the Beats Studio Pro and $70 off the Solo 4 at Amazon, but we expect to see more discounts later in November.

U.K. Black Friday price: There is £64 off the Powerbeats Pro 2 and £50 off the Powerbeats Fit at Amazon, but we expect to see more discounts later in November.

Should you buy AirPods now or wait for a better deal?

David Price / Foundry

With Black Friday approaching, we’d avoid paying full price unless you need AirPods immediately. But the sales now stretch across much of November, so you don’t necessarily need to wait for Black Friday itself. If an early offer is close to a model’s previous low, it can be worth taking: last year’s best deals frequently sold out, and popular offers could go quickly again.

Previous sale prices provide useful benchmarks. We’ve seen AirPods Pro 3 reach $169, while AirPods Max 2 fell to $399 during June Prime Day. An offer above those prices may still be worth considering, but a reduction from Apple’s regular price doesn’t automatically make it an exceptional deal.

For AirPods 5, waiting for a discount makes sense if you aren’t in a hurry: they didn’t receive a significant reduction during October Prime Day. With AirPods Max 2, we’d hold out for a substantial saving rather than pay full price.

Compare retailers, too. Amazon isn’t always cheapest: Walmart and Best Buy also compete on AirPods pricing, while Argos offered competitive U.K. deals last year. Our guide to the best time to buy AirPods has more advice on purchase timing.

Should you buy an old pair of AirPods?

Older-generation AirPods can be a good buy at the right clearance price. Compare their actual selling price with the discounted price of their replacement, rather than focusing on the percentage saving from an old launch price. A substantial discount can make an older pair worthwhile; a small difference may leave you sacrificing useful features for little saving.

AirPods 4 are harder to recommend now that AirPods 5 include Active Noise Cancellation as standard, starting at the same $129 price previously charged for AirPods 4 without ANC. Check which AirPods 4 version you’re buying—there were models with and without noise cancellation—and look for a substantial saving over AirPods 5.

AirPods Pro 2 remain worth considering if they’re significantly cheaper than Pro 3. However, the newer model improves fit, noise cancellation, and battery life, while adding heart-rate sensing. Compare their sale prices carefully: a strong Pro 3 discount could make the older pair’s clearance offer less attractive.

The original AirPods Max also need a substantial discount to justify choosing them over Max 2. The newer headphones add the H2 chip, improved noise cancellation, and features including Adaptive Audio and Conversation Awareness. Check the generation rather than relying on the charging port alone: the original AirPods Max were also sold in a USB-C version.

Buying older stock new is different from buying used or refurbished AirPods. For those pairs, check the stated condition, charging case, warranty, and returns policy, and buy from a reputable seller. Be cautious about battery condition and unusually low marketplace prices, since convincing counterfeits can resemble genuine AirPods. Our guide explains how to spot fake AirPods.

For more advice, see our AirPods buying guide and guide to the best time to buy AirPods.

AirPods deals to avoid

Foundry

Check exactly what an offer includes before comparing prices. Different charging-case packages can affect features and value, so make sure you’re comparing equivalent versions. Also check any spending requirements, contracts, or rebates attached to offers advertising “free” AirPods.

Judge the price against previous selling prices as well as the advertised discount. A large saving from the recommended retail price doesn’t necessarily mean a particularly good deal if retailers regularly charge less.

Check whether the listing is for a new, refurbished, or used pair. For used or refurbished AirPods, look for clear information about condition, warranty, and returns coverage. Battery condition deserves particular caution: a low purchase price may be less attractive if listening time has deteriorated.

Finally, check who is selling and dispatching your order, particularly when shopping through a marketplace. Unusually low prices from unfamiliar sellers warrant caution, since counterfeit AirPods can look convincing. Our guide explains how to tell if AirPods are fake.

How we choose AirPods deals

Macworld’s editors have decades of experience with Apple devices, and our recommendations draw on hands-on AirPods reviews. We consider sound quality, noise cancellation, comfort, battery life, and everyday use – not just the specifications or advertised saving.

Our testing helps us explain which features are worth paying for. For example, our AirPods Pro 3 review assessed how securely the redesigned ear tips stayed in place during exercise, checked battery life against Apple’s claims, and evaluated the heart-rate sensor. Our AirPods Max 2 review weighed their excellent sound and noise cancellation against drawbacks including weight and the Smart Case.

We combine those findings with current prices and previous lows to judge whether an offer represents good value. Our Best AirPods guide explains why the most expensive model isn’t necessarily the best choice for everyone: fit, listening habits, and the features you need all matter.

Which Apple Watch should you buy this Black Friday?

Apple Watch Series 12 – Our best overall choice

Apple

The Series 12 is the Apple Watch we recommend for most people. It combines Apple’s new Health Sensing System, more frequent heart-rate measurements, a Readiness score, and a tougher display with up to 24 hours of battery life.

A worthwhile Black Friday discount could make it an attractive purchase, but compare it with remaining Series 11 stock. The older model has the same quoted battery life, so a substantial saving may outweigh the newer health features.

U.S. Black Friday price: Amazon has already discounted the 42mm GPS Series 12 to $329, saving $70 and the best price we’ve ever seen. The 46mm version is also $70 off.

U.K. Black Friday price: We didn’t see Series 12 discounts during October Prime Day, and so far this November there have been no price drops, but we are hopeful. We have only seen discounts on older models so far.

Apple Watch Ultra 4 – Best for battery life and outdoor adventures

Apple

The Ultra 4 is our choice for endurance athletes, outdoor enthusiasts, and buyers who prioritize battery life. It offers up to 50 hours of normal use, satellite communication, precision dual-frequency GPS, diving features, and Apple’s new Health Sensing System.

It’s more watch than most people need. Compare it with the Ultra 3, though, which retains many of its outdoor features but has a shorter 42-hour battery-life rating.

Apple / Amazon

The SE 3 is the best-value option for buyers who want the core Apple Watch experience. It includes an always-on display, temperature sensing, fast charging, and the S10 chip, but lacks ECG, blood oxygen monitoring, and the newer Health Sensing System.

It remains part of Apple’s current lineup despite launching in 2025. A strong Black Friday offer could make it an excellent affordable purchase, although its previous discounts mean there’s little reason to settle for a token reduction.

U.S. Black Friday price: Both last Black Friday and October Prime Day brought the 40mm GPS model to $199 and the 44mm version to $229 – $50 below their regular prices. Already, the U.S. price is $199, $50 off at Amazon.

U.K. Black Friday price: Black Friday 2025 and October Prime Day brought the 40mm GPS model to £199 and the 44mm version to £229, saving £20. So far we haven’t seen any price drops for Black Friday 2026.

Apple’s deal: Apple will give $50 U.S. or £40 U.K. Apple Gift Card with an eligible Apple Watch SE 3 bought directly from Apple.

Apple

The Ultra 3 is worth considering if you want a rugged Apple Watch without paying for the latest model. It offers satellite communication, dual-frequency GPS, diving features, and up to 42 hours of battery life.

You give up the Ultra 4’s longer battery life and newer Health Sensing System. Compare their actual selling prices: the Ultra 3 needs to be sufficiently cheaper to justify choosing the older generation.

Apple Watch Series 11 – Best clearance option for everyday use

Apple Watch Series 11

The Series 11 could be a better-value everyday watch than the Series 12 if the price gap is large enough. It has the same quoted 24-hour battery life, although it lacks the newer Health Sensing System and Audio Intelligence features.

For buyers who don’t need those additions, a substantial clearance discount could be more useful than a small saving on the latest model.

U.K. Black Friday price: October Prime Day brought the 42mm Series 11 to £259 and the 46mm version to £299.
